description: BenchKeeper sets up Claude Code and Codex with one rules file and three skills. It is for developers who use Claude Code or Codex and want the same rules, skills and devcontainer setup in every repository. The skills ship as a plugin for both agents. setup.sh, which you run yourself, installs the rules, settings and plugins (BenchKeeper, Matt Pocock's skills, Ponytail) and asks before each change. setting-up-projects sets up each repository: devcontainer, AGENTS.md, stack skills at pinned versions. The following-dev-workflow skill sorts each request into a tier (quick, standard, full, research), so small changes skip the steps they do not need.

core.name: mattpocock/skills
core.role: his skills drive each SDLC phase (grilling, spec and tickets, tests first, code review, pull request)

prerequisites.name: GitHub CLI
prerequisites.for: issues and pull requests (optional, local branches without it)

prerequisites.name: Node.js and npm
prerequisites.for: Dev Containers CLI and skills CLI, user prefix such as `~/.local`

parallelTools.name: Orca
points: one git worktree per agent, the same prompt across agents
terminal splits, SSH remote worktrees, mobile app
`setup.sh` offers its `orca-cli` and `orchestration` skills after asking

every agent edit arrives as a diff you approve or reject

openhands.name: OpenHands
openhands.summary: A self-hosted agent server with a web UI that runs work without you at the terminal.
points: Each conversation can run in its own Docker container (`OH_CONVERSATION_RUNTIME=docker`), an isolation option BenchKeeper does not provide.
Runs its own agent or hosts Claude Code, Codex and Gemini CLI.
Automations on a schedule or on webhook events (GitHub, Slack, Linear), for example splitting GitHub issues into tasks.
Without a sandbox, the local agent has full access to your filesystem.
Unverified: whether agents inside its containers load the BenchKeeper rules and skills, which are installed on the host.

sdlc.requirements: Requests come from you, GitHub issues, Jira, Linear and other trackers, bug reports, reviews and Maintain findings. Only GitHub issues are automated.

steps.name: Understand
steps.tip: Reads the request, AGENTS.md and the code it touches, and picks the tier. Matt Pocock's on-ramps: triage for incoming issues, diagnosing-bugs for a broken behavior, wayfinder for work too big to see yet. Standard and full: plan mode, then a GitHub issue you approve.
steps.text: Read the request, `AGENTS.md` and the code the change touches, and pick the tier. Matt Pocock's on-ramps start here: `/triage` for issues you did not write, `diagnosing-bugs` for a broken behavior, `/wayfinder` for work too big to see the way yet. Standard and full tiers explore in plan mode first, then the agent drafts the issue (title, goal, acceptance criteria, tasks) and creates it after your approval.

steps.name: Specify
steps.tip: Standard: a plan of a few lines that names the test seams. Full: grilling settles the open questions. Work for several sessions: /to-spec and /to-tickets, which you run.
steps.text: Standard tier: a plan of a few lines in the reply that names the test seams. Full tier: `grilling` until the open questions are settled, `domain-modeling` records terms and decisions in `GLOSSARY.md` and ADRs. Work for several sessions: the agent suggests `/to-spec`, then `/to-tickets`, and waits for you to run them.

steps.name: Build
steps.tip: Every tier: a branch off the default branch. Runs the existing tests for the touched code, then builds with tdd at the agreed seams.
steps.text: Every tier: a branch `<type>/<issue>-<slug>`, or `<type>/<slug>` without an issue, never the default branch unless you say so. The existing tests that cover the touched code run first, then `tdd` at the agreed seams, ticket by ticket. Ponytail `full` for the smallest complete change. Targeted skills such as `diagnosing-bugs` load when the task matches. Full tier: work that drifts from the plan is discarded and restarted.

steps.name: Verify
steps.tip: Every tier: build, types, lint and tests in the devcontainer, each with its command and result. UI changes also in a browser. Standard and full: Matt Pocock's code-review checks standards and spec.
steps.text: Every tier: build, types, lint and tests inside the devcontainer, each reported with its command and result. UI changes also in a browser through Playwright MCP, in addition to the UI tests, never instead of them. Standard and full tiers: `mattpocock-skills:code-review` against the default branch with the issue as the spec (standards and spec), unless `/implement` just ran it with both of its sections.

steps.name: Ship
steps.tip: Standard and full: /code-review for correctness before push. Risky: /security-review. Draft pull request with a body from pr, checks, ready. You merge.
steps.text: Standard and full tiers: `/code-review` before `git push` (correctness). Risky changes get `/security-review` in any tier. Findings outside the task stop the push until you decide. Every tier: draft pull request with a body from `pr`, checks, ready. Merge only on your instruction. Unfinished work for another harness or person: state and next step on the issue or pull request, `/handoff` for the next session.

steps.name: Maintain
steps.tip: After a session that went sideways: retro. On request: /maintaining-repos (audit, debt, dependencies, docs drift, unused skills) and improve-codebase-architecture. Findings become new requests.
steps.text: After a session that went sideways: `/retro`. On request (`/maintaining-repos`), suggested after a milestone or about every 10 merged pull requests: Ponytail's audit and debt, dependency audit, docs drift, `/doctor prompt-audit`, `/skill-doctor`, `/improve-codebase-architecture`, `/triage`, repository hygiene. Findings become new requests.
